subject: Private deployment keystore custody and data flow — procurement questions
messages:
From: Hannah Lee <hlee@meditech-health.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood-inference.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@meditech-health.com>
Date: Mon, 7 Jun 2026 09:12:45 -0700
Subject: Private deployment keystore custody and data flow — procurement questions

Hi Sean,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement and InfoSec had a few follow-ups specific to a private deployment (VPC / on-prem) we expect to include in a draft SOW and DPA. The items we need clarity on are: 

- Customer-controlled keys: who holds the KEK/DEK in each deployment model?
- Operator access: in the private package what operational activities require Redwood operator access (e.g., node maintenance, debugging, break-glass)?
- Escrow / recovery: if we control keys, what is the recommended escrow or recovery mechanism?
- Data egress and export controls: can you confirm no model telemetry or logs leave our VPC without explicit consent?

I've attached our procurement checklist and an initial DPA template. Can you point us to a person who can verify the technical controls and suggest contract language? We have a tentative timeline to complete legal review by 2026-06-18.

Appreciate it —
Hannah Lee
Sr. Procurement Manager
Meditech Health

Attachments: Procurement_Checklist.xlsx (spreadsheet), MDT_DPA_template.docx (docx)

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood-inference.com>
To: Hannah Lee <hlee@meditech-health.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood-inference.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood-inference.com>
Date: Mon, 7 Jun 2026 10:03:02 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment keystore custody and data flow — procurement questions

Hannah —

Thanks for the clear list. Looping in Grace (security) and Dev (deployment/ops) to confirm specifics. High-level answers up front:

- Customer-controlled keys: supported. Customers can bring their own KEK via KMS or supply a wrapped key material; Redwood can integrate with customer KMS (AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, or on-prem HSM) so we never store unwrapped DEKs in our control plane.
- Operator access: for private packages we support an "operator-lite" model where routine infra ops are automated; operator access is limited to break-glass scenarios and requires multi-party approval and audit logs.
- Escrow/recovery: we recommend a customer-managed escrow with optional dual-control escrow (customer + third-party custodian). We can accept escrowed recovery tokens under contract if legally required.
- Telemetry/logs: by default, customer telemetry stays in their VPC. We can ship anonymized service metrics only with explicit opt-in and DPA language.

Please see Grace's notes below for concrete contract wording and an ops checklist. We'll prepare a short annex you can tuck into your DPA.

Next steps: Grace and Dev — can you draft annex language and an ops boundary matrix by EOD tomorrow (6/8)? I will follow up with a single redline to the DPA.

—Sean
Sean Gallagher
Head of Sales, Enterprise
Redwood Inference

Attachment: DPA_redline_20260607.pdf (preview of proposed redlines)

From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood-inference.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood-inference.com>, Hannah Lee <hlee@meditech-health.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood-inference.com>
Date: Mon, 8 Jun 2026 08:45:18 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment keystore custody and data flow — procurement questions

Hannah / Sean —

Below are the technical controls and suggested contract language snippets I recommend for the DPA annex. I'm keeping the language prescriptive so your legal team can copy/paste.

1) Key custody model (recommended):
- Customer holds KEK in their KMS; DEKs are generated in-deployment and wrapped with the KEK. Redwood will never have persistent access to unwrapped DEKs.
- Contract snippet: "Redwood shall not possess or retain master key material for Customer-managed KMS instances. All DEKs generated for model inference will be wrapped using Customer KEK and stored only within Customer-controlled infrastructure unless explicit written consent is provided."

2) Operator activities & break-glass:
- Allowed operator tasks: node provisioning, kernel updates, container restarts, and I/O troubleshooting.
- Disallowed without customer approval: retrieval of wrapped key material, live memory snapshots that may contain unwrapped keys, and pulling raw inference payloads off the VPC.
- Break-glass process: multi-party approval via ticketing (customer contact + Redwood security approver) + time-bound access + full forensic logging.
- Contract snippet: "Operator access to Customer private deployment is limited to the activities explicitly listed in Annex A. Any elevated access shall require prior written or documented telephonic approval and is subject to audit logging and post-incident review."

3) Escrow & recovery options:
- Option A: Customer-managed escrow (recommended).
- Option B: Third-party escrow with dual control (customer + custodian) — can be used if policy requires external recovery.
- Contract snippet: "Where Customer elects escrow arrangement, Redwood will accept escrow tokens under the conditions described in Annex B. Escrow retrieval requires written instruction from authorized Customer signatories."

4) Telemetry, logs, and egress controls:
- Default: telemetry for billing/health is aggregated and pushed to customer endpoints only. No plaintext inference payloads or prompt/response pairs leave the VPC.
- Optional: anonymized aggregated service metrics may be shared for capacity planning if Customer opts in.
- Contract snippet: "No inference inputs or outputs shall leave Customer VPC except as expressly permitted in writing. Aggregated telemetry may be transmitted for operational reasons only with Customer opt-in."

Attachments: Keystore_Handbook_v1.docx, Network_Flow_Diagram.png

If helpful I can produce a short Annex A and an operator playbook that matches the DPA wording.

—Grace
Grace O'Connor
Lead Security Engineer, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

From: Amit Desai <amit.desai@meditech-health.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood-inference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood-inference.com>
Cc: Hannah Lee <hlee@meditech-health.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@meditech-health.com>
Date: Tue, 9 Jun 2026 10:14:07 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment keystore custody and data flow — procurement questions

Grace, Sean —

Appreciate the thoroughness. A few clarifying asks from legal and our crypto team before we can proceed to contract redlines: 

1) Can you confirm whether live memory snapshots are explicitly blocked for all operator activities or only blocked unless customer provides a temporary exception? We need explicit language either way.
2) For the escrow option, can you name one or two third-party custodians Redwood has prior experience with (we have policy constraints for select custodians).
3) Please confirm retention windows for audit logs tied to operator access (we prefer 7 years for regulated records if feasible).

Procurement is also asking whether Redwood can provide a short statement for our SOW that you will not use models trained on our data for general Redwood model tune-ups. If there is a commercial/ops reason you can't commit to that, let us know and we will flag for legal.

If this looks good we'll push a DocuSign MoU to lock a short-term commitment while legal finishes the DPA review.

Thanks —
Amit Desai
Director, IT Security
Meditech Health

Attachment: MDT_Compliance_Notes.pdf (pdf)

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood-inference.com>
To: Amit Desai <amit.desai@meditech-health.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood-inference.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood-inference.com>
Cc: Kim Park <kimberly.park@redwood-inference.com>, Hannah Lee <hlee@meditech-health.com>
Date: Tue, 9 Jun 2026 16:03:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment keystore custody and data flow — procurement questions

Amit / team —

Quick answers and next steps: 

1) Live memory snapshots: blocked by default. We will only perform a memory snapshot with written, time-limited approval (ticket + multi-party sign-off). I'll ask Kim to confirm legal language that makes that explicit.

2) Escrow custodians: Redwood has worked with KeyCustody Partners and Fortify Escrow in past deals; we'll provide references and contact templates.

3) Audit log retention: Redwood can commit to a 7-year retention for operator-access audit records for regulated customers; we will include this in Annex C.

4) Model tuning: Redwood will not use Customer inference data to train or tune Redwood public models unless Customer provides explicit, contractual opt-in. We'll include a clause in the DPA Annex.

Action items: 
- Grace: finalize Annex A (operator activities + break-glass) and Annex C (audit log retention) by EOD 6/10.
- Dev: confirm and document the KMS integration steps and provide a short runbook for the escrow handoff.
- Kim: please confirm legal phrasing for memory-snapshot prohibition and the model-tuning carve-out.

I'll prepare the MoU DocuSign and share a draft link to expedite procurement's timeline.

Thanks everyone —
Sean
Head of Sales, Enterprise
Redwood Inference
